But he ansvvering sayd: All planting vvhich my heauenly father hath not planted, shal be rooted vp.
Let them alone: blinde they are, guides of the blinde. And if the blinde be guide to the blinde, both fall into the ditch.
And Peter answering sayd to him, Expound vs this parable.
But he sayd, Are you also as yet vvithout vnderstanding?
Do you not vnderstand, that al that entreth into the mouth, goeth into the belly, and is cast forth into the priuy?
But the things that proceede out of the mouth, come forth from the hart, and those things defile a man.
For from the hart come forth euil cogitations, murders, aduoutries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies.
These are the things that defile a man. but to eate vvith vnvvashen hands, doeth not defile a man. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> And <sc>IESVS</sc> vvent forth from thence and retired into the quarters of Tyre and Sidon.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Thursday the fifth weeke in Lent.

verses.text: And behold <cr>[1]</cr> a woman of Chanaan came forth out of those coastes, and crying out, sayd to him, Haue mercie vpon me, O lord the Sonne of Dauid: my daughter is sore vexed of a Deuil.
VVho ansvvered her not a word. And his Disciples came and besought him saying, Dimisse her: because she crieth out after vs:
And he ansvvering said: I was not sent but to the sheepe that are lost of the house of Israel.
But she came and adored him, saying, Lord, help me.
Who ansvvering, said: It is not good to take the bread of the Children, and to cast it to the dogges.
But she said, Yea lord: for the vvhelpes also eate of the crummes that fal from the table of their maisters.
Then <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering said to her, O vvoman, <na>[1]</na> great is thy faith: be it done to thee as thou vvilt: and her daughter was made hole from that houre. ⊢

notes.text: It were a straunge case that Christ should commend in this woman a sole faith without good workes, that is to say, a dead faith such as could not worke by loue, and which S. Iames doubted not to call the faith not of Christians but of Diuels. Aug. de Fid. & Op. c. 16.

verses.text: And when <sc>IESVS</sc> was passed from thence, he came beside the sea of Galilee: and ascending into the mountaine, sate there.
And there came to him great multitudes, hauing with them dumme persons, blinde, lame, feeble, and many others: and they cast them dovvne at his feete, and he cured them:
so that the multitudes marueled seeing the dumme speake, the lame vvalke, the blinde see: and they magnified the God of Israel.

And <cr>[1]</cr> <sc>IESVS</sc> called together his Disciples, and said: I pitie the multitude: because three dayes novv they continue vvith me, and haue not vvhat to eate: and dimisse them fasting I vvil not, lest they fainte in the vvay.
And the disciples say vnto him: vvhence then may vve gette so many loaues in the desert as to fil so great a multitude?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> sayd to them, Hovv many loaues haue you? but they sayd, Seuen, & a fevv litle fishes.
And he commaunded the multitude to sit dovvne vpon the ground.
And taking the seuen loaues & the fishes, and geuing thankes, he brake, & gaue to his disciples, and <na>[1]</na> the disciples gaue to the people.

notes.text: Here we see againe that the people must not be their owne caruers, nor receiue the Sacraments or other spiritual sustenance immediatly of Christ, or at their owne hand, but of their spiritual gouerners.

verses.text: And they did al eate, and had their fill. And that vvhich vvas left of the fragments they tooke vp, seuen baskets ful.
And there vvere that did eate, foure thousand men, beside children & women.
And hauing dimissed the multitude, he vvent vp into a boate, and came into the coastes of Magedan.

chapters.summary: The Pharisees of Hierusalem comming so farre to carpe him, he chargeth with a tradition contrarie to Gods commaundement. 10 And to the people he yeldeth the reason of that which they reproued: 15 and againe to his Disciples, shewing the ground of the Pharisaical washing (to witte, that meates otherwise defile the soule) to be false. 21 then he goeth aside to hide him self among the Gentils: where, in a woman he findeth such faith, that he is faine, lest the Gentils should before the time extort the whole bread, as she had a crumme, to returne to the Iewes. 34 where (al contrarie to those Pharisees) the common people seeke wonderfully vnto him. and he after he hath cured their diseased, feedeth 4000 of them with seuen loaues.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr> there came to him the Pharisees and Sadducees tempting: and they demaunded him to shew them a signe from heauen.
<cr>[1]</cr> But he answered & said to them, When it is euening, you say, It vvil be faire-wether, for the element is redde.
And in the morning, This day there vvil be a tempest, for the element doth glovve and lovvre. The face therfore of the element you haue skil to discerne: and the signes of times can you not?
The <cr>[1]</cr> naughtie and aduouterous generation seeketh for a signe: and there shal not a signe be giuen it, but the signe of Ionas the Prophet. And he left them and vvent avvay.
And <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen his disciples vvere come ouer the vvater, they forgot to take bread.
<cr>[1]</cr> Who said to them, Looke vvel and bevvare of the leauen of the Pharisees & Sadducees.
But they thought vvithin them selues saying, Because we tooke not bread.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> knovving it, said, Why do you thinke vvithin your selues O ye of litle faith, for that you haue not bread?
Do you not yet vnderstand, neither do you remember <cr>[1]</cr> the fiue loaues among fiue thousand men, and how many baskets you tooke vp?
neither the seuen loaues, among foure thousand men, and hovv many maundes you tooke vp?
Why do you not vnderstand that I said not of bread to you, Bevvare of the leauen of the Pharisees & Sadducees?
Then they vnderstoode that he said not they should bevvare of the leauen of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
<cr>[1]</cr> And <na>[2]</na> <sc>IESVS</sc> came into the quarters of Cæsarea Philippi: and he asked his disciples, saying, Whom say men that the Sonne of man is?

notes.text: The Gospel vpon SS. Peter and Paules day Iun. 29. And in Cathedra Petri Romæ, Ian. 18. & Antiochiæ Febr. 22. And Petri ad vincula Aug. 1. And on the day of the creation and coronation of the Pope, and on the Anniuersarie thereof.

verses.text: But they said, Some Iohn the Baptist, & othersome Elias, and others Hieremie, or one of the Prophets.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, But vvhom do you say that I am?
Simon Peter ansvvered & said, Thou art Christ the sonne of the liuing God.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering, said to him, Blessed art thou Simon bar-Iona: because flesh & bloud hath not reuealed it to thee, but my father vvhich is in heauen.
And I say to thee, That thou art [1][2] Peter: and vpon this Rocke vvil I build my Church, and the gates of hel shal not preuaile against it.

notes.text: That is, a Rocke.

verses.text: And I vvil giue to thee the keies of the kingdom of heauen. And vvhatsoeuer thou shalt binde vpon earth, it shal be bound also in the heauens: and whatsoeuer thou shalt loose in earth, it shall be loosed also in the heauens. ⊢
Then he commaunded his disciples that they should tel no body that he vvas <sc>IESVS CHRIST</sc>.

From that time <sc>IESVS</sc> began to shevv his disciples, that he must goe to Hierusalem, & suffer many things of the Ancients & Scribes & cheefe-Priestes, and be killed, and the third day rise againe.
And Peter taking him vnto him, began to rebuke him, saying, Lord, be it farre from thee, this shal not be vnto thee.
Who turning said to Peter, Goe after me <na>[1]</na> Satan, thou art a scandal vnto me: because thou sauourest not the things that are of God, but the things that are of men.

notes.text: This word in Hebrew signifieth an adversary, as 3. Reg.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Then <sc>IESVS</sc> said to his disciples, If any man wil come after me, let him denie him self, and take vp his crosse, and follow me.

notes.text: THE GOSPEL for a Martyr that is a bishop.

verses.text: For he that will saue his life, shal lose it. and he that shal lose his life for me, shal finde it.
For what doth it profite a man, if he gaine the vvhole vvorld, and sustaine the damage of his soule? Or vvhat permutation shal a man giue for his soule?
For the Sonne of man shal come in the glorie of his father with his Angels: and then vvil he render to euery man according to his vvorkes. ⊢
Amen I say to you, <cr>[1]</cr> there be some of them that stand here, that shal not taste death, til they see the Sonne of man comming in his kingdom.

notes.text: Cyr. l. 8. c. 12. Com. in Io.

chapters.summary: The obstinate Pharisees and Sadducees, as though his foresaid miracles were not sufficient to proue him to be Christ, require to see some one from heauen. 5 Wherevpon forsaking them, he warneth his disciples to beware of the leauen of their doctrine: 13 and Peter (the time now approching for him to goe into Iewrie to his Passion) for confessing him to be Christ, he maketh the Rocke of his Churche, geuing fulnes of Ecclesiastical power accordingly. 21 And after, he so rebuketh him for dissuading his Crosse and Passion, that he also affirmeth the like suffering in euery one to be necessarie to saluation.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> after six dayes <sc>IESVS</sc> taketh vnto him Peter and Iames and Iohn his brother, and bringeth them into a high mountaine apart:

notes.text: The Transfiguration of our Lord, celebrated in the Church the 6. of Aug. The Gospel of the said feast, & of the 2. Sunday in Lent: and on Imber Saturday before.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And he vvas transfigured before them. And his face did shine as the sunne: & his garments became vvhite as snow.
And behold there appeared to them Moyses and Elias talking vvith him.
And Peter answering, said to <sc>IESVS</sc>, Lord, it is good for vs to be here: if thou vvilt, let vs make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moyses, and one for Elias.
And as he was yet speaking, behold a bright cloude ouershadovved them. And loe a voice out of the cloude, saying. This is my vvelbeloued sonne, in vvhom I am vvel pleased: heare ye him.
And the disciples hearing it, fel vpon their face, and vvere sore afraid.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> came and touched them: and he said to them, Arise, and feare not.
And they lifting vp their eyes, saw no body, but only <sc>IESVS</sc>.
And as they descended from the mount, <sc>IESVS</sc> commaunded them, saying, Tel the vision to no body, til the Sonne of man be risen from the dead. ⊢
And his Disciples asked him, saying, What say the Scribes then, that <cr>[1]</cr> Elias must come first?
But he ansvvering, said to them, Elias in deede shal come, and restore al things.
And I say to you, that Elias is already come, and they did not knovv him, but vvrought on him vvhatsoeuer they vvould. So also the Sonne of man shal suffer of them.
Then the Disciples vnderstoode, that of Iohn the Baptist he had spoken to them.
And <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen he vvas come vnto the multitude, there came to him a man falling dovvne vpon his knees before him,
saying, Lord haue mercie vpon my sonne, for he is lunatike, and sore vexed: for he falleth often into the fire, and often into the vvater.
and I offered him to thy Disciples: and they could not cure him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered and said, O faithles and peruerse generation, hovv long shal I be vvith you? How long shal I suffer you? bring him hither to me.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> rebuked him, and the deuil vvent out of him, and the ladde was cured from that houre.
Then came the Disciples to <sc>IESVS</sc> secretely, and said, Why could not we cast him out?

<sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, because of your incredulity. for, amen I say to you, if you haue faith as a mustard seede, you shal say to this mountaine, Remoue from hence thither: and it shal remoue, and nothing shal be impossible to you.
But this kinde is not cast out but by prayer and fasting.
And <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen they conuersed in Galilee, <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, The Sonne of man is to be betraied into the hands of men:
and they shal kil him, and the third day he shal rise againe. And they were stroken sadde excedingly.
And vvhen they vvere come to Capharnaum, there came they that receiued the didrachmes, vnto Peter, and said to him, Your maister doth he not pay the <na>[1]</na> didrachmes?

notes.text: This stater was a double didrachme, and therfore was payed for two.

verses.text: He saith, Yes. And vvhen he vvas entered into the house, <sc>IESVS</sc> preuented him, saying, What is thy opinion Simon? The kings of the earth of vvhom receiue they tribute or cense? of their children, or of strangers?
And he said, Of strangers. <sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, Then the children are free.

But that vve may not scandalize them, goe thy vvaies to the sea, and cast a hooke: and that fish vvhich shal first come vp, take: and vvhen thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a <na>[1]</na> stater: take that, and giue it them for me and thee.

notes.text: This stater was a double didrachme, and therfore was payed for two.

chapters.summary: As he promised, he giueth them a sight of the glorie, vnto which Suffering doth bring: 9 and then againe doth inculcate his Passion. 14 A deuil also he casteth out which his Disciples could not for their incredulitie and lacke of praying and fasting. 22 being yet in Galilee, he reuealeth more about his Passion. 24 and the tribute that the Collectors exacted for al, he payeth for him self and Peter: declaring yet withal his freedom both by word and miracle.

verses.text: AT <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> that houre the Disciples came to <sc>IESVS</sc>, saying. Who, thinkest thou, is the greater in the kingdom of heauen?

notes.text: The Gospel on Michelmas day Septemb. 29. And vpon his Apparition Maij 8.

verses.text: And <sc>IESVS</sc> calling vnto him a litle childe, set him in the middes of them,
and said, Amen I say to you, vnles you be conuerted, and become as litle children, you shal not enter into the kingdom of heauen.
VVhosoeuer therfore shal humble him self as this <na>[1]</na> litle childe, he is the greater in the kingdom of heauen.

notes.text: Humility, innocencie, simplicity, commended to vs in the state and person of a childe.

verses.text: And he that shal receiue one such litle childe in my name, receiueth me.

And <cr>[1]</cr> he that shal scandalize one of these litle ones that beleeue in me, it is expedient for him that a milstone be hanged about his necke, and that he be drovvned in the depth of the sea.
VVo be to the vvorld for scandals. for it is necessary that scandals do come: but neuerthelesse vvo to that man by vvhom the scandall commeth.

And <cr>[1]</cr> if thy hand, or thy foote scandalize thee: cut it of, and cast it from thee. It is good for thee to goe in to life maimed or lame, rather then hauing tvvo hands or tvvo feete to be cast into euerlasting fire.
And if thine eye scandalize thee, plucke him out, and cast him from thee: It is good for thee hauing one eye to enter into life, rather then hauing tvvo eyes to be cast into the hel of fire.
See that you despise not one of these litle ones: for I say to you that their Angels, in heauen alvvaies do see the face of my father vvhich is in heauen.
For <cr>[1]</cr> the Sonne of man is come to saue that vvhich vvas perished.
<cr>[1]</cr> Hovv thinke you? If a man haue an hundred sheepe, and one of them shal goe astray: doth he not leaue ninetie nine in the mountaines, and goeth to seeke that which is straied?
And if it chaunce that he finde it: amen I say to you, that he reioyceth more fore that, then for the ninetie nine that vvent not astray.
Euen so it is not the vvil of your father, vvhich is in heauen, that one perish of these litle ones.
<cr>[1]</cr> But <na>[2]</na> if thy brother shal offend against thee, goe, and rebuke him betvvene thee and him alone. If he shal heare thee, thou shalt gaine thy brother.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Tuesday the 3 weeke in Lent.

verses.text: And if he vvil not heare thee, ioyne vvith thee besides, one or tvvo: that in the mouth of <cr>[1]</cr> tvvo or three vvitnesses euery vvord may stand.
And if he vvil not heare them, [1] tel the Church. And if he vvil not heare the Church, let him be to thee as the heathen and the Publican.

notes.text: That is (as S. Chrysostom here expoundeth it) tell the Prelates and cheefe Pastours of the Church: for they haue iurisdiction to binde and loose such offenders, by the wordes folowing v. 18.

verses.text: Amen I say to you, whatsoeuer you shal binde vpon earth, shal be bound also in heauen: and vvhatsoeuer you shal loose vpon earth, shal be loosed also in heauen.
Againe I say to you, that if two of you shal <na>[1]</na> consent vpon earth, concerning euery thing vvhatsoeuer they shal aske, it shal be done to them of my father vvhich is in heauen.

notes.text: Al ioyning together in the vnity of Christes Churche in Councels and Synods, or publike prayers, is of more force then of any particular man.

verses.text: For vvhere there be tvvo or three gathered in my name, there am I in the middes of them.
Then came Peter vnto him and said, <cr>[1]</cr> Lord, how often shal my brother offend against me, and I forgiue him? vntil seuentimes?
<sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, I say not to thee <cr>[1]</cr> vntil seuen times: but vntil seuentie times seuen times. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> Therfore is the kingdom of heauen likened to a man being a king, that vvould make an account vvith his seruants.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 21 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: And vvhen he began to make the account, there vvas one presented vnto him that ovved him ten thousand talents.
And hauing not vvhence to repay it, his lord commaunded that he should be sold, and his wife and children, and all that he had, and it to be repayed.
But that seruant falling dovvne, besought him, saying, Haue patience tovvard me, and I vvil repay thee all.
And the lord of that seruant moued vvith pitie, dimissed him, and the dette he forgaue him.
And vvhen that seruant vvas gone forth, he found one of his felow-seruants that did ovve him an hundred pence: and laying hands vpon him thratled him, saying, Repay that thou owest.
And his felovv seruant falling dovvne, besought him, saying, Haue patience tovvard me, and I vvil repay the all.
And he would not: but vvent his vvay, and cast him into prison, til he repayed the dette.
And his felow-seruants seeing vvhat vvas done, vvere very sorie, and they came, and told their lord al that vvas done.
Then his lord called him: and he said vnto him, Thou vngratious seruant, I forgaue thee al the dette because thou besoughtest me:
oughtest not thou therfore also to haue mercie vpon thy felow-seruant, euen as I had mercie vpon thee?
And his lord being angrie deliuered him to the tormenters, vntil he repayed al the dette.
So also shal my heauenly father doe to you, if you forgiue not euery one his brother from your hartes. ⊢

chapters.summary: To his Disciples he preacheth against ambition the mother of Schisme: 7 foretelling both the author whosoeuer he be, and also his folowers, of their wo to come. 10 and shewing on the contrary side, how precious Christian soules are to their Angels, to the Sonne of man, and to his Father. 15 charging vs therfore to forgiue our brethren, when also we haue iust cause against them, be it neuer so often, and to labour their saluation by al meanes possible.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr> it came to passe, vvhen <sc>IESVS</sc> had ended these vvordes, he departed from Galilee, & came into the coastes of Ievvrie beyond Iordan,
and great multitudes folovved him: and he cured them there.
<na>[1]</na> And there came to him the Pharisees tempting him, and saying, Is it lavvful for a man to dimisse his vvife, for euery cause?

notes.text: The Gospel for Marriage, and upon S. Agatha's day. Feb. 5.

verses.text: Who ansvvering, said to them, Haue ye not read, that he which did [1] `make' from the beginning, [2] made them male and femal? And he said.

notes.text: make man

verses.text: [1] For this cause, man shal leaue father and mother, and shal cleaue to his vvife: and they tvvo shal be in one flesh.
Therfore novv they are not two, but one flesh. That therfore vvhich God hath ioyned together, let not man separate. ⊢
They say to him, Why then <cr>[1]</cr> did Moyses commaund to giue a bil of diuorce, and to dimisse her?
He saith to them, Because Moyses for the hardnes of your hart permitted you to dimisse your vviues: but from the beginning it vvas not so.

And I say to you, that <cr>[1]</cr> Whosoeuer shal dimisse his vvife, but for fornication, and shal mary an other, doth committe aduoutrie: and he that shal mary her that is dimissed, committeth aduoutrie.
His disciples say vnto him, If the case of a man vvith his vvife be so, it is not expedient to mary.
Who said to them, Not al <na>[1]</na> take this vvord, but they to vvhom it is giuen.

notes.text: χωροῦσι. capiunt.

verses.text: For there are eunuches which vvere borne so from their mothers vvombe: and there are eunuches vvhich were made by men: and there are eunuches, vvhich haue gelded them selues for the kingdom of heauen. He that can take, let him take. ⊢
Then <cr>[1]</cr> were litle children presented to him, that he should impose hands vpon them & pray. And the disciples rebuked them.
But <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, Suffer the litle children, and stay them not from comming vnto me: for the kingdom of heauen is for such.
And when he had imposed hands vpon them, he departed from thence.
And <cr>[1]</cr> behold one came and said to him, Good Maister, vvhat good shal I doe that I may haue life euerlasting?
Who said to him, What askest thou me of good? One is good, God. But <na>[1]</na> if thou vvilt enter into life, keepe the commaundements.

notes.text: I see not (saith S. Augustine) why Christ should say, If thou wilt haue life euerlasting, keepe the commaundements: if without obseruing of thē, by only faith one might be saued. Aug. de Fid. & op. c. 15.

verses.text: He saith to him, Which? And IESVS said, [1] Thou shalt not murder, Thou shalt not committe aduoutrie, Thou shalt not steale, Thou shalt not beare false vvitnes,
Honour thy father and thy mother, [1] Thou shalt loue thy neighbour as thy self.
The yong man saith to him, Al these haue I kept from my youth: vvhat is yet vvanting vnto me?
<sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, If thou vvilt be perfect, goe, sel the things that thou hast, & giue to the poore, and thou shalt haue treasure in heauen: and come, folovv me.
And when the yong man had heard this vvord, he vvent avvay sad: for he had many possessions.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to his disciples, Amen I say to you, that a rich man shal hardely enter into the kingdom of heauen.
And againe I say to you, it is easier for a camel to passe through the eye of a nedle, <na>[1]</na> then for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heauen.

notes.text: S. Marke expoundeth it thus, riche men trusting in their riches, ca. 10, 24.

verses.text: And vvhen they had heard this, the disciples marueled very much, saying, Who then can be saued?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> beholding, said to them. With men this is impossible: but vvith God al things are possible.
<na>[1]</na> Then Peter ansvvering, said to him, Behold vve haue left al things, & haue folovved thee: what therfore shal we haue?

notes.text: The Gospel upon the Conversion of S. Paul. Ian. 25. Also within the Octave, and in a votive Mass of SS. Peter & Paul, and for holy abbots.

verses.text: And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, Amen I say to you, that you which haue folowed me, in the regeneration, vvhen the Sonne of man shal sitte in the seate of his maiestie, you also shal sitte vpon twelue seates, iudging the tvvelue tribes of Israel.

And euery one that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or <na>[1]</na> wife, or children, or landes for my names sake: shal receiue an hundred fold, and shal possesse life euerlasting. ⊢

notes.text: Hereof is gathered that the Apostles among other things left their wiues also to folow Christ. Hiero. li. 1. aduers. Iouin.

verses.text: And <cr>[1]</cr> many shal be first, that are last: and last, that are first.

chapters.summary: He answereth the tempting Pharisees, that the case of a man with his wife shalbe (as in the first institution it was) vtterly indissoluble, though for one cause he may be diuorced. 10 And therevpon to his Disciples he highly commendeth Single life for heauen. 13 He wil haue children come vnto him. 16 He sheweth what is to be done to enter into life euerlasting: 20 What also, for a rich man to be perfect: 27 As also what passing reward they shal haue which follow that his counsel of perfection: 29 yea though it be but in some one peece. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: The fourth part of this Gospel, Christ's coming into Jury toward his Passion.

verses.text: Jericho, he giveth sight unto two blind.
<sc>THE</sc> <na>[1]</na> kingdom of heauen is like to a man that is an housholder vvhich went forth early in the morning to hire workemen into his vineyard.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the Sunday of Septuagesme.

verses.text: And hauing made couenant vvith the Workemen for a penie a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
And going forth about the third houre, he savv other standing in the market place idle,
and he said to them, Goe you also into the vineyard: and that vvhich shal be iust, I vvil giue you.
And they vvent their vvay. And againe he vvent forth about the sixt & the ninth houre: and did likewise.
But about the eleuenth houre he vvent forth and found other standing, & he saith to them, What stand you here al the day idle?
They say to him, Because no man hath hired vs. He saith to them, Goe you also into the vineyard.
And vvhen euening vvas come, the lord of the vineyard saith to his bailife, Call the vvorkemen, and pay them their hire, beginning from the last euen to the first.
Therfore vvhen they vvere come that came about the eleuenth houre, they receiued euery one a penie.
But vvhen the first also came, they thought that they should receiue more: and they also receiued euery one a penie.
And receiuing it they <na>[1]</na> murmured against the good man of the house,

notes.text: The Iewes are noted for enuying the vocation of the Gentiles, and their reward equal with thē selues.

verses.text: saying, These last haue continued one houre: and thou hast made them equal to vs that haue borne the burden of the day and the heates.
But he ansvvering said to one of them, Frende, I doe the no vvrong: didst thou not couenant vvith me for a penie?
Take that is thine, and goe: I vvil also giue to this last euen as to thee also.
Or, is it not lavvful for me to do that I vvil? is thine eye naught, because I am good?
So shal the last, be first: and the first, last. For many be called, but fevv elect. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And <sc>IESVS</sc> going vp to Hierusalem, tooke the tvvelue disciples secretly, and said to them,

notes.text: The Gospel upon Wednesday the 2. week in Lent. And in a votive Mass of the holy Cross.

verses.text: Behold vve goe vp to Hierusalem, and the Sonne of man shal be deliuered to the cheefe priestes and to the Scribes, and they shal condemne him to death,
and shal deliuer him to the Gentiles to be mocked, & scourged, & crucified, and the third day he shal rise againe. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> Then came to him the mother of the sonnes of Zebedee vvith her sonnes, adoring and desiring some thing of him.

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Jame's day. Iul. 25. And S. John's ante portam Latinam Maij 6.

verses.text: Who said to her, What wilt thou? She saith to him, Say that these my tvvo sonnes may sitte, one at thy right hand, and one at thy left hand in thy kingdom.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering, said, You knovv not vvhat you desire. Can you drinke of the cuppe that I shal drinke of? They say to him, We can.
He saith to them, My cuppe in deede you shal drinke of: but to sitte at my right hand and left, is not mine to giue to you: but to vvhom it is prepared of my father. ⊢
And the ten hearing it, vvere displeased at the tvvo brethren.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> called them vnto him, and said, <cr>[1]</cr> You knovv that the princes of the gentiles <na>[2]</na> ouerrule them: and they that are the greater, exercise povver against them.

notes.text: Superiority is not here forbidden among Christians, neither Ecclesiastical nor temporal: but heathenish tyranny is forbidden, and humility commended.

verses.text: It shal not be so among you. but vvhosoeuer vvil be the greater among you, let him be your minister:
and he that vvil be first among you, shal be your seruant.
Euen as the Sonne of man is not come to be ministred vnto, but to minister, and to giue his life a redemption for many. ⊢
And <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen they vvent out from Iericho, a great multitude folovved him.
And behold tvvo blinde men sitting by the vvay side, heard that <sc>IESVS</sc> passed by, and they cried out saying, Lord, haue mercie vpon vs, sonne of Dauid.
And the multitude rebuked them that they should hold their peace. But they cried out the more, saying, Lord, haue mercie vpon vs, sonne of Dauid.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> stoode, and called them, and said, VVhat vvil ye that I doe to you?
They say to him, Lord, that our eies may be opened.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> hauing compassion on them, <na>[1]</na> touched their eies. And immediatly they savv, and folovved him.

notes.text: Our Saviour who always could, and often did cure the diseased, by his only will, or word, here gave sight to these blind men, by touching their eyes with his holy hand.

chapters.summary: To shew how through Gods grace the Iewes shalbe ouerrunne of the Gentils, although they beginne after, he bringeth a parable of men working soner and later in the vineyard, but the later rewarded in the end euen as the first. 17 He reuealeth more to his Disciples touching his passion: 20 Bidding the ambitious two suiters to thinke rather of suffering with him: 24 And teaching vs (in the rest of his Disciples) not to be greeued at our Ecclesiastical Superiors, considering they are (as he was him self) to toile for our Saluation. 29 Then going out of Iericho, he geueth sight vnto two blind.

verses.text: consequently their irreparable damnation that shall ensue thereof. [1]

notes.text: THE FIFTH part, of the Holy weeke of his Passion in Hierusalem.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> vvhen they drevv nigh to Hierusalem, and vvere come to Beth-phagee vnto Mount-oliuet, then <sc>IESVS</sc> sent two disciples,

notes.text: The Gospel on Palme Sunday before the benediction of the Palmes.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> saying to them, Goe ye into the tovvne that is against you, and immediatly you shal finde an asse tied and a colt vvith her: loose them & bring them to me:

notes.text: PALME SVNDAY.

verses.text: and if any man shal say ought vnto you, say ye, that our Lord hath neede of them: and forthvvith he vvil let them goe.
And this vvas done that it might be fulfilled vvhich vvas spoken by the Prophet, saying,
[1] Say ye to the daughter of Sion, Behold thy king commeth to thee, meeke, & sitting vpon an asse and a colt the fole of her that is vsed to the yoke.
And the disciples going, did as <sc>IESVS</sc> commaunded them.
And they brought the asse and the colt: and laide their garments vpon them, and made him to sit thereon.
And a very great multitude spred their garments in the vvay: and others did cut boughes from the trees, and stravved them in the vvay:
and the multitudes that vvent before and that folovved, cried, saying, [1] Hosanna to the sonne of Dauid: blessed is he that commeth in the name of our Lord. ⊢ Hosanna in the highest.
<na>[1]</na> And when he vvas entred Hierusalem, the vvhole citie vvas moued, saying, Who is this?

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Tuesday the first weeke in Lent.

verses.text: And the people said, This is <sc>IESVS</sc> the Prophet, of Nazareth in Galilee.

And <cr>[1]</cr> <sc>IESVS</sc> entred into the temple of God, and cast out al that <na>[2]</na> sold and bought in the temple, and the tables of the bankers, and the chaires of them that sold pigeons he ouerthrevve:

notes.text: How much the abuse of Churches by merchandising, walking, or other profane occupying of them, displeaseth God, here we may see.

verses.text: and he saith to them, It is vvritten, [1] My house shal be called the house of prayer: but you haue made it a denne of theeues.
And there came to him the blinde, and the lame in the temple: and he healed them.
And the cheefe priestes & Scribes seeing the maruelous things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, & saying, Hosanna to the sonne of Dauid: they had indignation,
and said to him, Hearest thou vvhat these say? And IESVS said to them, Very vvel. haue you neuer read, [1] That out of the mouth of infants and sucklings thou hast perfited praise?
And leauing them, he vvent forth out of the citie into Bethania, and remained there. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> And in the morning returning into the citie, he vvas an hungred.

notes.text: MVNDAY.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And seeing a certaine <na>[2]</na> figtree by the vvay side, he came to it: and found nothing on it but leaues only, and he saith to it, Neuer grovv there fruite of thee for euer. And incontinent the figtree vvas vvithered.

notes.text: The Iewes hauing the wordes of the law, and not the deedes, were the figtree ful of leaues, and void of fruite. Aug. de verb. Do. Serm. 44.

verses.text: And the disciples seeing it, marueled saying, How is it vvithered incontinent?

<cr>[1]</cr> And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering said to them, Amen I say to you, <na>[2]</na> if you shal haue faith, and stagger not, not only that of the figtree shal you doe, but and if you shal say to this mountaine, Take vp and throvv thy self into the sea, it shal be done.

notes.text: b TUESDAY.

verses.text: And al things vvhatsoeuer you shal aske in prayer beleeuing, you shal receiue.

And vvhen he vvas come into the temple, there came to him as he vvas teaching, the cheefe Priests and auncients of the people, saying, <cr>[1]</cr> In vvhat povver doest thou these things? and vvho hath giuen thee this povver?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering said to them, I also vvil aske you one vvord: vvhich if you shal tell me, I also vvil tel you in vvhat povver I doe these things.
The Baptisme of Iohn vvhence vvas it? from heauen, or from men? But they thought vvithin them selues, saying,
If vve shal say from heauen, he vvil say to vs, vvhy then did you not beleeue him? but if vve shal say from men: vve feare the multitude. for al hold Iohn as a Prophet.
And ansvvering to <sc>IESVS</sc> they said, We know not. He also said to them, Neither do I tel you in vvhat povver I doe these things.
But vvhat is your opinion? A certaine man had tvvo sonnes: and comming to the first, he said, Sonne, goe vvorke to day in my vineyard.
And he answering, said, I wil not. But afterward moued vvith repentance he vvent.
And comming to the other, he said likevvise. And he ansvvering, said, I goe Lord, and he vvent not.
VVhich of the tvvo did the fathers vvil? They say to him, The first. <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, Amen I say to you, that the Publicans and vvhoores goe before you into the kingdom of God.
For Iohn came to you in the vvay of iustice: and you did not beleeue him. but the publicans and vvhoores did beleeue him: but you seeing it, neither haue ye had repentance aftervvard, to beleeue him.

<cr>[1]</cr> An other parable heare ye: A man there vvas an housholder vvho <na>[2]</na> planted a vineyard, and made a hedge round about it, and digged in it a presse, and builded a tovvre, and let it out to husbandmen: and vvent forth into a strange countrie.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon friday the second weeke in Lent.

verses.text: And vvhen the time of fruites drevve nigh, he sent his seruants to the husbandmen, to receiue the fruites thereof.
And the husbandmen apprehending his seruants, one they beat, an other they killed, and an other they stoned.
Againe he sent other seruants moe then the former: and they did to them likevvise.
And last of al he sent to them his sonne, saying, They vvil reuerence my sonne.
But the husbandmen seeing the sonne, said vvithin them selues, This is the heire, come, let vs kil him, and vve shal haue his inheritaunce.
And apprehending him they cast him forth out of the vineyard, and killed him.
When therfore the lord of the vineyard shal come, vvhat vvil he doe to those husbandmen?
They say to him, The naughtie men he vvil bring to naught: and his vineyard he vvil let out to other husbandmen, that shal render him the fruite in their seasons.

IESVS saith to them, Haue you neuer read in the Scriptures, [1] The stone which the builders reiected, the same is made into the head of the corner? By our lord was this done, and it is maruelous in our eyes.
Therfore I say to you, that the kingdom of God shal be taken avvay from you, and shal be giuen to a nation yelding the fruites thereof.
And <cr>[1]</cr> he that falleth vpon this stone, shal be broken: and on whom it falleth, it shal al to bruise him.
And vvhen the cheefe Priestes and Pharisees had heard his parables, they knevve that he spake of them.
And seeking to lay hands vpon him, they feared the multitudes: because they held him as a Prophet. ⊢

chapters.summary: Being now come to the place of his Passion, he entereth with humility and triumph together: 12 Sheweth his zeale for the house of God ioyned with great maruels. 15 And to the Rulers he boldly defendeth the acclamations of the children. 18 He curseth also that fruitles leafie tree: 23 auoucheth his power by the witnes of Iohn: 28 and foretelleth his in two parables their reprobation (with the Gentils vocation) for their wicked deserts, 42 and consequently their irreparable damnation that shal ensue therof.

verses.text: <sc>AND <na>[1]</na> IESVS</sc> ansvvering, spake againe in parables to them, saying:

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 19 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: The kingdom of heauen is likened to a man being a king, vvhich made a mariage to his sonne.
And he sent his seruants to call them that vvere inuited to the mariage: and they vvould not come.
Againe he sent other seruants, saying, Tel them that vvere inuited, Behold I haue prepared my dinner: my beeues and fatlings are killed, and al things are ready: come ye to the mariage.
But they neglected: and vvent their vvaies, one to his farme, and an other to his merchandise:
and the rest laid hands vpon his seruants, and spitefully intreating them, murdered them.
But vvhen the king had heard of it, he vvas vvroth, and sending his hostes, destroied those murderers, and burnt their citie.
Then he saith to his seruants, The mariage in deede is ready: but they that vvere inuited, vvere not vvorthie.
Goe ye therfore into the high vvayes: and vvhosoeuer you shal finde, call to the mariage.
And his seruants going forth into the vvayes, gathered together al that they found, <na>[1]</na> bad and good: and the mariage vvas filled vvith ghestes.

notes.text: Not only good men be within the church, but also euil men. against the Heretikes of these daies.

verses.text: And the king vvent in to see the ghestes: and he savv there a man not attired in a vvedding garment.
And he saith to him, Frende, hovv camest thou in hither not hauing a vvedding garment? But he vvas dumme.
Then the king said to the vvaiters, Binde his hands and feete, and cast him into the vtter darkenes: there shal be vveeping & gnashing of teeth.
For many be called, but fevv elect. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> Then the Pharisees departing, consulted among them selues for to entrappe him in his talke.

And they send to him their disciples vvith the Herodians, saying, Maister, vve knovv that thou art a true speaker, and teachest the vvay of God in truth, neither carest thou for any man. for thou doest not respect the person of men:
tel vs therfore vvhat is thy opinion, is it lawful to giue tribute to Cæsar, or not?
But <sc>IESVS</sc> knovving their naughtines, said, What do you tempt me Hypocrites?
Shevv me the tribute coine. And they offred him a penie.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, Whose is this image and superscription?
They say to him, Cæsars. Then he saith to them, Render therfore the things that are Cæsars, to Cæsar: and the things that are Gods, to God.
And hearing it they marueled, and leauing him vvent their vvaies.
<cr>[1]</cr> That day there came to him the Sadducees, that say there is no resurrection: and asked him,
saying, Maister, Moyses said, [1] If a man die not hauing a childe, that his brother marie his wife, and raise vp seede to his brother.
And there vvere vvith vs seuen brethren: and the first hauing maried a wife, died: and not hauing issue, left his vvife to his brother.
In like maner the second and the third euen to the seuenth.
And last of al the vvoman died also.
In the resurrection therfore vvhose vvife of the seuen shal she be? for they al had her.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> answering, said to them, You do erre, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the povver of God.
For in the resurrection neither shal they marie nor be maried: but are as the Angels of God in heauen.
And concerning the resurrection of the dead, haue you not read that wich was spoken of God saying to you,
[1] I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob? He is not God of the dead, but of the liuing.
And the multitudes hearing it, marueled at his doctrine.
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> But the Pharisees hearing that he had put the Sadducees to silence, came together:

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 17 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: and one of them a doctor of law asked of him, tempting him,
Maister, vvhich is the great commaundement in the lavv?
IESVS said to him, [1] Thou shalt loue the lord thy God from thy whole hart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole minde.
This is the greatest and the first commaundement.
And the second is like to this, [1] Thou shalt loue thy neighbour as thyself.
On these tvvo commaundements dependeth the vvhole Lavv and the Prophets.
And <cr>[1]</cr> the Pharisees being assembled, <sc>IESVS</sc> asked them
saying, What is your opinion of Christ? Whose sonne is he? They say to him, Dauids.
He saith to them, Hovv then doth Dauid in spirit cal him Lord, saying,
[1] The Lord said to my Lord, sitte on my right hand, vntil I put thine enemies the foote stole of thy feete?
If Dauid therfore call him Lord, how is he his sonne?
And no man could ansvver him a vvord: neither durst any man from that day aske him any more. ⊢

chapters.summary: Yet by one other parable he foresheweth the most deserued reprobation of the earthly and persecuting Iewes, and the gratious vocation of the Gentils in their place. 15 Then he defeateth the snare of the Pharisees and Herodians about paying tribute to Cæsar. 23 He answereth also the inuention of the Sadducees against the Resurrection: 34 and a question that the Pharisees aske to pose him: turning and posing them againe, because they imagined that Christ should be no more then a man: 46 and so he putteth al the busy Sectes to silence.

verses.text: <sc>THEN <na>[1]</na> IESVS</sc> spake to the multitudes and to his disciples,

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Tuesday the second weeke in Lent.

verses.text: saying, Vpon the chaire of Moyses haue sitten the Scribes and the Pharisees.
Al things therfore vvhatsoeuer they shal say to you, obserue ye and doe ye: but according to their vvorkes doe ye not, for they say and doe not.
For <cr>[1]</cr> they binde heauy burdens & importable: and put them vpon mens shoulders: but vvith a finger of their ovvne they vvil not moue them.
But they doe al their vvorkes, for to be seen of men. for they make brode their <cr>[1]</cr> phylacteries, and enlarge their <na>[2]</na> fringes.

notes.text: These phylacteries were peeces of parchement, wherein they wrote the ten commaundements, and folded it, and caried it on their forehead before their eies, imagining grosly and superstitiously, that so they fulfilled that which is said Deu. 6, They shal be immoueable before thine eies. Hiero. in 23 Mat.

verses.text: And they loue the first places at suppers, and <cr>[1]</cr> the first chaires in the Synagogs,
and salutations in the market-place, and to be called of men, Rabbi.
But be not you called Rabbi. for one is your maister, and al you are brethren.
And call none father to your self vpon earth: for one is your father, he that is in heauen.
Neither <cr>[1]</cr> be ye called maisters: for one is your maister, Christ.
He that is the greater of you, shal be your seruiteur.
And he that exalteth him self, shal be humbled: and he that humbleth him self, shal be exalted. ⊢
But wo to you Scribes & Pharisees, hypocrites: because you shut the kingdom of heauen before men. For your selues do not enter in: & those that are going in, you suffer not to enter.
Wo to you Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: because you <cr>[1]</cr> deuoure vvidovves houses, praying long prayers. for this you shal receiue the greater iudgement.

Wo to you Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: because you goe round about the sea and the land, to make one proselyte: and vvhen he is made, you make him the childe of hel double more then your selues.
Wo to you blinde guides, that say, Whosoeuer shal svveare by the temple, it is nothing: but he that shal svveare by the gold of the temple, is bound.
Ye foolish and blinde, for vvhether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?
And vvhosoeuer shal svveare by the altar, it is nothing: but vvhosoeuer shal sweare by the gift that is vpon it, is bound.
Ye blinde, for vvhether is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?
He therfore that sweareth by the altar, sweareth by it and by al things that are vpon it:
and vvhosoeuer shal svveare by the temple, sweareth by it and by him that dvvelleth in it:
and he that sweareth by heauen, svveareth by the throne of God & by him that sitteth thereon.

Wo to you Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: because you tithe mint, and anise, and cummin, and haue left the weightier things of the law, iudgement, and mercie, and faith. these things you ought to haue done, & not to haue omitted those.
Blinde guides, that straine a gnat, and swallow a camel.
Wo to you Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: because you make cleane that on the outside of the cuppe and dish: but vvithin <na>[1]</na> <alt>`you are ful</alt>' of rapine and vncleannes.

notes.text: `they are ful

verses.text: Thou blinde Pharisee, first make cleane the inside of the cuppe and the dish, that the outside may become cleane.
Wo to you Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: because you are like to vvhited sepulchres, vvhich outvvardly appeare vnto men beautiful, but vvithin are ful of dead mens bones, and al filthines.
So you also outvvardly in deede appeare to men iust: but invvardly you are ful of hypocrisie and iniquitie.
Wo to you Scribes and Pharisees, ye hypocrites: because you build the Prophets sepulchres, and garnish the moniments of iust men,
and say: If we had been in our fathers dayes, vve had not been their felovves in the bloud of the Prophets.
Therefore you are a testimonie to your ovvne selues, that you are the sonnes of them that killed the Prophets.
And fil you vp the measure of your fathers.
You serpents, vipers broodes, hovv vvil you flee from the iudgement of hel?

<na>[1]</na> Therfore behold I send vnto you Prophets and vvise men and scribes, and of them you shal kil & crucifie, and of them you shal scourge in your Synagogs, and persecute from citie into citie:

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Steven's day Decemb. 26. And his Invention Aug. 3.

verses.text: that vpon you may come al the iust bloud that vvas shed vpon the earth, from the bloud of <cr>[1]</cr> Abel the iust euen vnto the bloud of <cr>[2]</cr> Zacharias the sonne of Barachias,vvhom you murdered betvvene the temple and the altar.
Amen I say to you, al these things shal come vpon this generation.

<cr>[1]</cr> Hierusalem, Hierusalem, vvhich killest the Prophets, and stonest them that vvere sent to thee, hovv often vvould I gather together thy children as the henne doth gather together her chickens vnder her vvinges, and thou <na>[2]</na> vvouldest not?

notes.text: Free wil.

verses.text: Behold, your house shal be left desert to you.
For I say to you, you shal not see me from hence forth til you say, Blessed is he that commeth in the name of our Lord. ⊢

chapters.summary: The Scribes and Pharisees after al this, continuing stil incorrigible, although he wil haue the doctrine of their Chaire obeied, yet against their workes (and namely their ambition) he openly inueigheth, crying to them eight woes for their eightfold hypocrisie and blindnes: 34 and so concluding with the most worthy reprobation of that persecuting generation and their mother-citie Ierusalem with her Temple.

verses.text: <sc>AND <cr>[1]</cr> IESVS</sc> being gone out of the temple, vvent. And his disciples came to shevv him the buildings of the temple.
And he answering said to them, Do you see al these things? Amen I say to you, there shal not be left here a stone vpon a stone that shal not be destroied.

<na>[1]</na> And vvhen he vvas sitting vpon Mount-oliuet, the disciples came to him secretly, saying: Tel vs, vvhen shal these things be? and vvhat shal be the signe of thy comming, and of the consummation of the vvorld?

notes.text: The Gospel for a votiue Masse in time of warre. and for many Martyrs.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering, said to them, Bevvare that no man seduce you:

notes.text: TVESDAY night.

verses.text: for many shal come in my name saying, I am Christ: and they shal seduce many.
For you shal heare of vvarres, & bruites of vvarres. See that ye be not troubled. for these things must be done: but the end is not yet.
for nation shal rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shal be pestilences, and famines, and earth-quakes in places,
and al these things are the beginnings of sorovves. ⊢
Then <cr>[1]</cr> shal they deliuer you into tribulation, and shal kil you: and you shal be odious to al nations for my names sake.
And then many shal be scandalized: and they shal deliuer vp one an other: and they shal hate one an other.
And many <na>[1]</na> falseprophets shal rise: and shal seduce many.

notes.text: There were in the people false Prophetes, as among you also shal be lying Maisters, which shal bring in Sectes of perdition. 2. Pet. 2.

verses.text: And because iniquitie shal abound: the charitie of many shal waxe cold.
But he that shal perseuêre to the end, he shal be saued. ⊢
And this Gospel of the kingdom shal be preached in the vvhole vvorld, for a testimonie to al nations, and then shal come the consummation.
[1] Therfore vvhen you shal see [2] the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, standing in the holy place (he that readeth, let him vnderstand)

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the last Sunday after Pentecost. · Dan. 9, 27.

verses.text: then they that are in Ievvrie, let them flee to the mountaines:
and he that is on the house-toppe, let him not come dovvne to take any thing out of his house:
and he that is in the field, let him not goe backe to take his coate.
And vvo to thē that are vvith childe, and that giue sucke in those dayes.
But pray that your flight be not in the vvinter or on the Sabboth.
For there shal be then great tribulation, such as hath not been from the beginning of the vvorld vntil novv, neither shal be.
And vnles those daies had been shortened, no flesh should be saued: but for the elect the daies shal be shortened.
Then if any man shal say vnto you, Loe <na>[1]</na> here is Christ, or there: do not beleeue him.

notes.text: Whosoeuer draweth Christ or his Church from the Communion and felowship of al Nations Christened, to one corner, towne, or Countrie, beleeue him not. Aug. de vnit. Ec. c. 3.

verses.text: For there shal rise false-Christes and false-Prophets, and shal shevv great signes and vvonders, so that the elect also (if it be possible) may be induced into errour.
Loe I haue foretold you.
If therfore they shal say vnto you, Behold he is in the desert: goe ye not out: behold in the closets, beleeue it not.
For as lightening commeth out of the east, and appeareth euen into the vvest, so shal also the aduent of the sonne of man be.
VVheresoeuer the body is, thither shal the egles also be gathered together.

And immediatly after the tribulation of those dayes <cr>[1]</cr> the sonne shal be darkened, and the moone shal not giue her light, and the starres shal fal from heauen, and the powers of heauen shal be moued:

and then shal appeare <na>[1]</na> the signe of the Sonne of man in heauen: and then shal al tribes of the earth bevvaile: and they shal see the Sonne of man comming in the cloudes of heauen vvith much povver and maiestie.

notes.text: This signe of the Sonne of man, is the holy Crosse, which then shal appeare to the Iewes to their confusion. Chrys. in Mat. ho. 77. It shal be no lesse confusion to Heretikes that can not abide the signe thereof.

verses.text: And he shal send his Angels vvith a trumpet, and a great voyce: and they shal gather together his elect from the foure vvindes, from the furthest partes of heauen euen to the endes thereof.
And of the figtree learne a parable: When novv the bough thereof is tender, and the leaues come forth, you know that sommer is nigh.
So you also, vvhen you shal see these things, knovv ye that it is nigh euen at the doores.
Amen I say to you, that this generation shal not passe, til al these things be done.
Heauen and earth shal passe, but my wordes shal not passe. ⊢
But of that day and houre no body knovveth, neither the Angels of heauen, but the Father alone.
And as <cr>[1]</cr> in the dayes of Noe, so shal also the comming of the Sonne of man be.
For as they vvere in the dayes before the floud, eating and drinking, marying and giuing to mariage, euen vnto that day in which Noe entred into the arke,
and knevve not til the floud came, and tooke them al: so also shal the comming of the Sonne of man be.
Then two shal be in the field: one shal be taken, and one shal be left.
tvvo vvomen grinding in the mill: one shal be taken, and one shal be left.
Watch therfore because you knovv not vvhat houre your Lord vvil come.
<cr>[1]</cr> But this knovv ye, that <na>[2]</na> if the good man of the house did knovv vvhat houre the theefe vvould come, he would surely vvatch, and vvould not suffer his house to be broken vp.

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Clement martyr his day Novemb. 23. And for some Confessors Bishops.

verses.text: Therfore be you also ready, because at what houre you knovv not, the Sonne of man vvil come.
Who, thinkest thou, is a faithful and vvise seruant, vvhom his lord hath appointed ouer his familie, to giue them meate in season?
Blessed is that seruant, vvhom vvhen his lord commeth, he shal finde so doing.
Amen I say to you, that ouer al his goods shal he appoint him. ⊢
But if that naughtie seruant shal say in his hart, My lord is long a comming:
and shal beginne to strike his felow-seruants, and eateth, and drinketh vvith drunkards:
the lord of that seruant shal come in a day that he hopeth not, and an houre that he knovveth not,
and shal deuide him, and appoint his portion vvith the hypocrites: there shal be vveeping and gnashing of teeth.

chapters.summary: To his Disciples (by occasion of Hierusalem and the Temples destruction) he foretelleth, 4. what things shalbe before the consummation of the world, as specially, 14. the Churches ful preaching vnto al nations: 15. then, what shalbe in the very consummation, to wit, Antichrist with his passing great persecution and seduction, but for a short time: 29. then incontinent, the Day of iudgement to our great comfort in those miseries vnder Antichrist. 35. As for the moment, to vs it perteineth not to know it, 37. but rather euery man to watch, that we be not vnprouided when he commeth to ech one particularly by death.

verses.text: <sc>THEN</sc> <na>[1]</na> shal the kingdom of heauen be like to ten virgins: which taking their lampes vvent forth to meete the bridegrome and the bride.

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Catharine's day. Novemb. 25. And for some other holy Virgins.

verses.text: And fiue of them were foolish, and fiue wise.
but the fiue foolish, hauing taken their lampes, did not take oile with them:
but the vvise did take oile in their vessels vvith the lampes.
And the bridegrome tarying long, they slumbered all and slept.
And at midnight there vvas a clamour made, Behold the bridegrome commeth, goe ye forth to meete him.
Then arose al those virgins: and they trimmed their lampes.
And the foolish said to the vvise, Giue vs of <na>[1]</na> your oile: because our lampes are going out.

notes.text: If we be not in the fauour of God, and haue not our owne merites, we shal not be holpen by other mens deserts at the day of iudgement.

verses.text: The vvise ansvvered, saying, Lest peraduenture there suffise not for vs and you, goe rather to them that sel: and bie for your selues.
And vvhiles they vvent to bie, the bridegrome vvas come: and they that vvere ready, entred with him to the mariage, and the gate was shut.
But last of al come also the other virgins, saying: Lord, Lord, open to vs.
But he ansvvering said, Amen I say to you, I knovv you not.
Watch ye therfore, because you knovv not the day nor the houre. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr> For <na>[2]</na> euen as a man going into a strange countrie, called his seruants, and deliuered them his goods.

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Nicolas' day Decemb. 6. and for some other Confessors Bishops.

verses.text: And to one he gaue fiue talents, and to an other tvvo, and to an other one, to euery one according to his propre facultie: and immediatly he tooke his iourney.
And he that had receiued the fiue talents, vvent his vvay, and occupied vvith the same, and gained other fiue.
Likevvise also he that had receiued the tvvo, gained other tvvo.
But he that had receiued the one, going his vvay digged into the earth, and hid his lords money.
But after much time the lord of those seruants commeth, and made a count vvith them.
And there came he that had receiued the fiue talents, and offred other fiue talents, saying, Lord fiue talents thou didst deliuer me, behold <na>[1]</na> I haue gained other fiue besides.

notes.text: Free will with Gods grace doth merite.

verses.text: His lord said vnto him: Wel fare thee good and faithful seruant, because thou hast been faithful ouer a fevv things, I wil place thee ouer many things: enter into the ioy of thy lord.
And there came also he that had receiued the tvvo talents, and said, Lord tvvo talents thou didst deliuer me: behold I haue gained other tvvo.
His lord said to him, Wel fare thee good and faithful seruant: because thou hast been faithful ouer a fevv things, I vvil place thee ouer many things, enter into the ioy of thy lord. ⊢
And he also that had receiued the one talent, came forth, and said, Lord, I knovv that thou art a hard man, thou reapest vvhere thou didst not sovv: and gatherest vvhere thou strawedst not:
and being afraid I vvent, and hid thy talent in the earth: behold loe here thou hast that vvhich thine is.
And his lord ansvvering, said to him: <na>[1]</na> Naughtie and sloughtful seruant, thou didst knovv that I reape vvhere I sow not, & gather vvhere I stravved not:

notes.text: A terrible example for al such as do not employ the very least gift of God, to his glorie.

verses.text: thou oughtest therfore to haue committed my money to the bankers, and comming I might haue receiued mine ovvne vvith vsurie.
Take ye avvay therfore the talent from him, and giue it him that hath ten talents.
For to <cr>[1]</cr> euery one that hath shal be giuen, and he shal abound: but from him that hath not, that also vvhich he seemeth to haue, shal be taken avvay from him.
And the vnprofitable seruant cast ye out into the vtter darknesse. There shal be vveeping and gnashing of teeth.
<na>[1]</na> And when the sonne of man shal come in his maiestie, and al the Angels vvith him, then shal he sitte vpon the seate of his maiestie:

notes.text: The Gospel vpon munday the first weeke of Lent.

verses.text: and al nations shal be gathered together before him, and he shal separate them one from an other, as the pastor separateth the sheepe from the goates:
and shal set the sheepe at his right hand, but the goates at his left.
Then shal the king say to them that shal be at his right hand, Come ye blessed of my father, possesse you the kingdom <na>[1]</na> prepared for you from the foundation of the vvorld.

notes.text: This kingdom then is prepared for those onely that do good workes: as Christ also signifieth els where, saying that it is not in his power to giue it otherwise. See the annot. c. 20, 23.

verses.text: for I was an hungred, and you gaue me to eate: I vvas a thirst, and you gaue me to drinke.
I vvas a stranger, and you tooke me in: naked, and you couered me: sicke, and you visited me. I vvas in prison, and you came to me.
Then shal the iust ansvver him, saying: Lord, vvhen did vve see thee an hungred, and fed thee: a thirst, and gaue thee drinke?
and vvhen did vve see thee a stranger, and tooke thee in? or naked, and couered thee?
or vvhen did vve see thee sicke or in prison: and came to thee?
And the king ansvvering, shall say to them, Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.
Then he shal say to them also that shal be at his left hand, Get ye avvay from me you cursed into fire euerlasting, vvhich vvas prepared for the Deuil and his angels.
for I vvas an hungred, and you gaue me not to eate: I vvas a thirst, and you gaue me not to drinke.
I Was a stranger, and you tooke me not in: naked, and you couered me not: sicke, and in prison, and you did not visite me.
Then they also shall ansvver him, saying, Lord, vvhen did vve see thee an hungred, or a thirst, or a stranger, or naked, or sicke, or in prison: and did not minister to thee?
Then he shal ansvver them, saying, Amen I say to you, as long as you did it not to one of these lesser, neither did you it to me.
And these shal goe into punishment euerlasting: but the iust, into life euerlasting. ⊢

chapters.summary: Continuing his Sermon, he bringeth two parables, of ten Virgins, and of Talents, to shew how it shalbe in Domesday with the Faithful that prepare, and that prepare not them selues. 31. Then also without parables he sheweth that such Faithful as doe workes of mercy, shal haue for them life euerlasting: and such as doe not, euerlasting damnation.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> it came to passe, when <sc>IESVS</sc> had ended al these vvordes, he said to his Disciples,

notes.text: The Passion according to S. Matthew in these two Chapters, is the Gospel at Masse vpon Palme Sunday.

verses.text: You knovv that after tvvo dayes shal be Pasche, and the Sonne of man shal be deliuered to be crucified.
<na>[1]</na> Then were gathered together the cheefe Priestes and auncients of the people into the court of the high priest, vvho vvas called Caiphas:

notes.text: TENEBRÆ-Wednesday.

verses.text: and they consulted hovv they might by some vvile apprehend <sc>IESVS</sc>, and kil him.
But they said, Not on the festiual day, lest perhaps there might be a tumult among the people.
And <cr>[1]</cr> when <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas in Bethania in the house of Simon the Leper,
there came to him a vvoman hauing an alabaster-boxe of pretious ointment, and povvred it out vpon his head as he sate at the table.
And the Disciples seeing it, had indignation saying, Whereto is this wast?
for this might haue been sold for much, and giuen to the poore.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> knovving it, said to them: Why do you molest this vvoman? for she hath vvrought a good vvorke vpon me.
For the poore you haue alvvayes vvith you: but me you haue not alvvayes.
For she in povvring this ointment vpon my body: hath done it to burie me.
Amen I say to you, vvheresoeuer this Gospel shal be preached in the vvhole vvorld, that also vvhich she hath done, <na>[1]</na> shal be reported for a memorie of her.

notes.text: Hereby we learne that the good workes of Saincts are to be recorded and set forth to their honour in the Church after their death. Whereof rise their holy daies and Commemorations.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> Then went one of the Tvvelue, vvhich vvas called Iudas Iscarioth, to the cheefe Priestes,
and said to them, What vvil you giue me, and I vvil deliuer him vnto you? But they appointed vnto him thirtie peeces of siluer.
And from thenceforth he sought opportunitie to betray him.
<cr>[1]</cr> And <na>[2]</na> the first day of the Azymes the Disciples came to <sc>IESVS</sc>, saying, Where vvilt thou that we prepare for thee to eate the Pasche?

notes.text: MAVNDY thursday.

verses.text: But <sc>IESVS</sc> said, Goe ye into the citie to a certaine man: and say to him, The Maister saith, My time is at hand, vvith thee do I make the Pasche vvith my Disciples.
And the Disciples did as <sc>IESVS</sc> appointed them, and they prepared the Pasche.
But vvhen it vvas euen, he sate downe vvith his tvvelue Disciples.
And vvhile they vvere eating, he said: Amen I say to you, that one of you shal betray me.
And they being very sad, began euery one to say, Is it I Lord?
But he ansvvering said, <cr>[1]</cr> He that dippeth his hand vvith me in the dish, he shal betray me.
The Sonne of man in deede goeth as it is vvritten of him: but vvo be to that man, by vvhom the Sonne of man shal be betrayed. It vvere good for him, if that man had not been borne.
And Iudas that betrayed him, ansvvering said, Is it I Rabbi? He saith to him, Thou hast said.
And <cr>[1]</cr> vvhiles they vvere at supper, <sc>IESVS</sc> tooke bread, and blessed, and brake: and he gaue to his Disciples, and said, Take ye, and eate: <sc>THIS IS MY BODY</sc>.
And taking the chalice, he gaue thankes: and gaue to them, saying: Drinke <na>[1]</na> ye al of this.

notes.text: See the margent note Mar. 14, 23.

verses.text: <sc>For THIS IS MY BLOVD OF THE NEVV TESTAMENT, VVHICH SHAL BE SHED FOR MANY VNTO REMISSION OF SINNES</sc>.
And I say to you, I vvil not drinke from henceforth of this fruite of the vine, vntil that day vvhen I shal drinke it vvith you nevv in the kingdom of my father.
<na>[1]</na> And an hymne being said, they vvent forth vnto Mount-oliuet.

notes.text: THVRSDAY night.

verses.text: [1] Then IESVS saith to them, Al you shal be scandalized in me, in this night. For it is vvritten, [2] I vvil strike the Pastor, and the sheepe of the flocke shal be dispersed.

notes.text: The NOCTVRNE of Mattins in the Churches Seruice, answereth to this night part of our Sauiours Passion. and so consequently the other Canonical houres to the rest. · Zach. 13, 7.

verses.text: But after I shal be risen againe, I vvil goe before you into Galilee.
And Peter answering, said to him, Although al shal be scandalized in thee, I vvil neuer be scandalized.
<sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, Amen I say to thee, that in this night before the cocke crovv, thou shalt denie me thrise.
<cr>[1]</cr> Peter saith to him, Yea though I should die vvith thee, I vvil not denie thee. Likevvise also said al the Disciples.
Then <sc>IESVS</sc> commeth vvith them into a village called Gethsémani: and he said to his Disciples, Sitte you here til I goe yonder, and pray.
And taking to him Peter and the tvvo sonnes of Zebedee, he began to vvaxe sorowful and to be sad.
Then he saith to them: My soul is sorovvful euen vnto death: stay here, and vvatch vvith me.
And being gone forvvard a litle, he fel vpon his face, praying, and saying, My Father, if it be possible, let this chalice passe from me. neuerthelesse not as I vvil, but as thou.
And he commeth to his Disciples, and findeth them sleeping, and he saith to Peter, Euen so? Could you not vvatch one houre vvith me?
Watch ye, and pray that ye enter not into tentation. The spirit in deede is prompt, but the flesh vveake.
Againe the second time he vvent, and prayed, saying, My Father, if this chalice may not passe, but I must drinke it, thy vvil be done.
And he commeth againe, and findeth them sleeping: for their eyes vvere become heauy.
And leauing them, he went againe: and he prayed the third time, saying the self same vvord.
Then he commeth to his Disciples, and saith to them, Sleepe ye now and take rest: behold the houre approcheth, and the Sonne of man shal be betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Rise, let vs goe: behold he approcheth that shal betray me.
<cr>[1]</cr> As he yet spake, behold Iudas one of the Tvvelue came, and vvith him a great multitude vvith swordes and clubbes, sent from the cheefe Priestes and the auncients of the people.
And he that betrayed him, gaue them a signe, saying, Whomsoeuer I shal kisse, that is he, hold him.
And forthvvith comming to <sc>IESVS</sc>, he said, Haile Rabbi. And he kissed him.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, Freend, vvhereto art thou come? Then they drevve neere, and laid hands on <sc>IESVS</sc>, and held him.
And behold one of them that vvere vvith <sc>IESVS</sc>, stretching forth his hand, drevve out his svvord: and striking the seruant of the high Priest, cut of his eare.
Then <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, Returne thy sword into his place: for al that take the sword, shal perish vvith the sword.
Thinkest thou that I cannot aske my Father: and he vvil giue me presently more then tvvelue legions of Angels?
How then shal the scriptures be fulfilled, that so it must be done?

In that houre <sc>IESVS</sc> said to the multitudes: You are come out as it vvere to a theefe vvith swordes and clubbes to apprehend me: I sate daily vvith you teaching in the temple: and you laid no hands on me.
And al this vvas done, that the scriptures of the Prophets might be fulfilled. Then the disciples al leauing him, fled.
But they taking hold of <sc>IESVS</sc>, led him to Caiphas the high Priest, vvhere the Scribes and auncients vvere assembled.
And Peter folovved him a farre of, euen to the court of the high Priest. And going in he sate vvith the seruants, that he might see the end.
And the cheefe Priestes and the vvhole Councel sought false vvitnes against <sc>IESVS</sc>, that they might put him to death:
and they found not, vvhereas many false witnesses had come in. And last of al there came tvvo false vvitnesses:
and they said, <cr>[1]</cr> This man said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and after three dayes to reedifie it.
And the high Priest rising vp, said to him: Answerest thou nothing to the things vvhich these do testifie against thee?
But <sc>IESVS</sc> held his peace. And the high Priest said to him: I adiure thee by the liuing God, that thou tel vs if thou be Christ the sonne of God.

<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, Thou hast said. neuertheles I say to you, hereafter you shal see <cr>[1]</cr> the Sonne of man sitting on the right hand of the povver of God, and comming in the cloudes of heauen.
Then the high Priest rent his garments, saying, He hath blasphemed, vvhat neede vve witnesses any further? behold, novv you haue heard the blasphemie,
how thinke you? But they ansvvering said, He is guilty of death.
Then did they spit on his face, and buffeted him, and other smote his face vvith the palmes of their hands,
saying, Prophecie vnto vs O Christ: vvho is he that strooke thee?
But Peter sate vvithout in the court: and there came to him one vvenche, saying: Thou also vvast vvith <sc>IESVS</sc> the Galilean.
But he denied before them all, saying, I wot not vvhat thou sayest.
And as he vvent out of the gate, an other vvenche savv him, and she saith to them that vvere there, And this felow also vvas vvith <sc>IESVS</sc> the Nazarite.
And againe he denied vvith an othe, That I knovv not the man.
And after a litle they came that stoode by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art of them: for euen thy speache doth bewray thee.
<na>[1]</na> Then he began to curse and to sweare that he knevve not the man. And incontinent the cocke crevve.

notes.text: To this time the Laudes do answer in the Church's Service.

verses.text: And Peter remembred the vvord of <sc>IESVS</sc> vvhich he had said, Before the cocke crovv, thou shalt deny me thrise. And going forth, he wept bitterly.

chapters.summary: To the Councel of the Iewes, Iudas by occasion of Marie Magdalens ointment, doth sell him for litle. 17. After the Paschal lambe, 26. he giueth them that bread of life (promised Io. 6,) in a mystical Sacrifice or Separation of his Body and Bloud. 31. And that night he is after his prayer 47. taken of the Iewes men, Iudas being their captaine: and forsaken of the other eleuen for feare: 57. is falsely accused, and impiously condemned of the Iewes Councel, 67. and shamefully abused of them: 69. and thrise denied of Peter: Al, euen as the Scriptures and him self had often foretold

verses.text: being buried, they to make all sure, set soldiers to keep his sepulcher.
<sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> vvhen morning vvas come, al the cheefe Priestes and auncients of the people consulted together against <sc>IESVS</sc>, that they might put him to death.

notes.text: PRIME, or Hora prima, in the Church's Service.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> And they brought him bound and deliuered him to Ponce Pilate the President.

notes.text: GOOD FRIday.

verses.text: Then Iudas that betrayed him, seeing that he vvas condemned, repenting him, returned the thirtie siluer peeces to the cheefe Priestes and auncients,
saying, I haue sinned, betraying iust bloud. But they said, what is that to vs? looke thou to it.
And casting dovvne the siluer peeces in the temple, he departed: and vvent and hanged him self with an halter.
And the cheefe Priestes hauing taken the siluer peeces, said, It is not lavvful to cast them into the <na>[1]</na> Córbana: because it is the price of bloud.

notes.text: This Corbana was a place about the Temple, which receiued the peoples gifts or offerings. See Mar. 12, v. 42.

verses.text: And after they had consulted together, they bought vvith them the potters field, to be a burying place for strangers.
For this cause that field vvas called Hacéldama, that is, the field of bloud, euen to this present day.
Then vvas fulfilled that vvhich vvas spoken by Ieremie the Prophet, saying, [1] And they tooke the thirtie peeces of siluer, the price of the priced, vvhom they did price of the children of Israel:
and they gaue them into the potters field, as our Lord did appoint to me.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> stoode before the President, and the President asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Iewes? <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, Thou sayest.
And vvhen he vvas accused of the cheefe Priestes and auncients, he answered nothing.
Then Pilate saith to him, Doest thou not heare hovv many testimonies they alleage against thee?
And he ansvvered him not to any vvord: so that the President did maruel excedingly.
<na>[1]</na> And vpon the solemne day the President had accustomed to release vnto the people one prisoner vvhom they vvould.

notes.text: HORA TERTIA in the Churches Seruice.

verses.text: And he had then a notorious prisoner, that vvas called Barabbas.
They therfore being gathered together, Pilate said: whom vvil you that I release to you, Barabbas, or <sc>IESVS</sc> that is called Christ?
For he knevve that for enuie they had deliuered him.
And as he vvas sitting in place of iudgment, his vvife sent vnto him, saying: Haue thou nothing to doe vvith that iust man. for I haue suffred many things this day in my sleepe for him.
But the cheefe Priestes and auncients persuaded the people, that they should aske Barabbas, and make <sc>IESVS</sc> avvay.
And the President ansvvering, said to them: Whether vvil you of the tvvo to be released vnto you? But they said, Barabbas.
Pilate saith to them, what shal I doe then vvith <sc>IESVS</sc> that is called Christ? They say al, Let him be crucified.
The President said to them, why vvhat euil hath he done? But they cried the more, saying, Let him be crucified.

And Pilate seeing that he nothing preuailed, but rather tumult vvas tovvard: taking vvater he vvashed his hands before the people, saying, I am innocent of the bloud of this iust man: looke you to it.
And the vvhole people ansvvering, said, His bloud be vpon vs, and vpon our children.
Then he released to them Barabbas, and hauing scourged <sc>IESVS</sc>, deliuered him vnto them for to be crucified.
Then the Presidents souldiars taking <sc>IESVS</sc> into the Palace, gathered together vnto him the vvhole band:
<cr>[1]</cr> and stripping him, put a scarlet cloke about him,
and platting a crovvne of thornes, put it vpon his head, and a reede in his right hand. And bovving the knee before him, they mocked him, saying, Haile King of the Iewes.
And spitting vpon him, they tooke the reede, and smote his head.
And after they had mocked him, they tooke of the cloke from him, and put on him his ovvne garments, and led him avvay to crucifie him.
And in going they found a man of Cyréne, named Simon: him they forced to take vp his crosse.
<na>[1]</na> And they came into the place that is called Golgotha, vvhich is, the place of Caluarie.

notes.text: HORA SEXTA in the Churches Seruice.

verses.text: And they gaue him vvine to drinke mingled vvith gall. And vvhen he had tasted, he vvould not drinke.

And after they had crucified him, they deuided his garments, casting lottes: that it might be fulfilled vvhich vvas spoken by the Prophet, saying: [1] They deuided my garments among them: and vpon my vesture they did cast lottes.
And they sate and vvatched him.
And they put ouer his head his cause vvritten, <sc>THIS IS IESVS THE KING OF THE IEWES</sc>.
Then vvere crucified vvith him tvvo theeues: one on the right hand, and one on the left.
And they that passed by, blasphemed him, vvagging their heades,
and saying, Vah, thou that destroyest the temple of God, and in three daies doest reedifie it: saue thine ovvne self: if thou be the sonne of God, come dovvne from the Crosse.
In like maner also the cheefe Priestes With the Scribes and auncients mocking, said:
He saued other: him self he can not saue: if he be the King of Israel, let him novv come dovvne from the Crosse, and vve vvil beleeue him.
<cr>[1]</cr> He trusted in God: let him novv deliuer him if he vvill: for he said, That I am the sonne of God.
And the self same thing the theeues also that were crucified vvith him, reproched him vvithal.
And from the sixt houre, there vvas darkenesse made vpon the vvhole earth, vntil the ninthe houre.
And about the ninthe houre IESVS cried vvith a mighty voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lamma-sabacthani? that is, My God, my God, vvhy hast thou forsaken me?
And certaine that stoode there and heard, said, He calleth Elias.
And incontinent one of them running, tooke a sponge, & filled it vvith vinegre: and put it on a reede, and gaue him to drinke.
And other said, Let be, let vs see vvhether Elias come to deliuer him.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> againe crying vvith a mighty voice, yelded vp the ghost.
<na>[1]</na> And be hold the vele of the temple vvas rent in tvvo peeces, from the toppe euen to the botome. and the earth did quake, and the rockes vvere rent,

notes.text: HORA nona, in the Church's Service.

verses.text: and the graues vvere opened: and many bodies of the saincts that had slept, rose.
And they going forth out of the graues after his resurrection, came into the holy citie: and appeared to many.
